clinician.trajectory_summary: A 30-year-old man presented with dry cough, exertional dyspnoea, disseminated pigmented rash, extensive cervical lymphadenopathy, severe oedema, and cachexia. Initial chest radiograph showed extensive airspace opacification. Blood tests revealed low albumin, elevated CRP, ferritin, and D-dimer. HIV serology was positive with a CD4 count of 116 cells/μL and a high viral load. CT imaging showed nodular interlobular and peribronchial interstitial thickening in the lungs, diffuse thickening of major fissures, and innumerable multifocal lytic bone lesions. A CT-guided biopsy of an iliac crest lesion confirmed Kaposi Sarcoma, demonstrating spindle cell proliferation positive for CD34 and HHV-8. This evidence supports a diagnosis of widely disseminated HIV-associated Kaposi Sarcoma.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with respiratory symptoms (dry cough, exertional dyspnoea), disseminated pigmented rash, extensive non-tender cervical lymphadenopathy, severe lower limb and scrotal oedema, and marked cachexia.
Initial chest radiograph showed extensive airspace opacification involving upper-mid and lower zones bilaterally.
Initial blood tests showed low albumin, elevated C-reactive protein, slightly raised ferritin, and grossly elevated D-dimer.
HIV serology was positive, with a total CD4+ T-helper lymphocyte count of 116 cells/μL and a viral load of 87,272 copies/mL.
CT imaging demonstrated nodular interlobular and peribronchial interstitial thickening, diffuse thickening of the major fissures, and innumerable, multifocal lytic bone lesions.
CT-guided biopsy of an iliac crest bony lesion demonstrated bone infiltrated by spindle cell proliferation, strongly positive for CD34 and HHV-8 on immunohistochemistry, confirming Kaposi Sarcoma.
